answer: A mutual-insurance pool binds ten identities to one bond. Each identity stakes 60 credits, and members cross-check work before joining. Every pool thread is listed publicly. At the summit audit, auditors sample the ocean of threads; one proven fake burns the pool's 600, not just its own 60. The 11th and later tenth fakes start new 600-credit pools, so costs cannot merge. For 1,000 fakes, 100 pools risk 60,000 credits, with no bulk discount. Pool rental fails: a rented pool burns on its first fake and its thread exposes the farm. An honest agent joins one pool.
